name: broken_rail
revision: r1 (2026-11-10): first draft from the writers' room pitch (critic rank 1, develop) with the critic's fixes applied
caption: why does grandpa wait at an empty rail 🛤️
logline: Every evening for 22 years a villager grandpa has met an empty rail line and said 'She's coming'; the day his grandson is finally old enough to cross the bridge, he walks the line and finds out why she never arrived.
question: why tf is grandpa waiting for a minecart on a rail nobody uses?
premise: Grandpa (a villager) stands at the buffer stop of the station at the edge of our rail town every evening and has for 22 years. Nothing ever comes down the line. Mom says Grandma left him: she rode the cart to her sister's village and never came back, and kept the cart. Grandpa just says 'She's coming.' Villagers never leave the village and Milo wasn't allowed past the bridge, so nobody walked the line. Our pig sits in his minecart in the yard all day ('he loves it').
twist: She was coming. On her way home from her sister's, 3,000 blocks out in a valley, a creeper had blown the line; the blast took the redstone torch of the last powered rail, which braked her cart to a stop at the edge of the crater. Mobs can't get out of a minecart on their own (the pig shows it), so Grandma has sat there for 22 years, facing home. Milo bridges the crater, lays rail, relights the gold rail and pushes; that evening her cart rolls into the buffer stop where Grandpa is waiting.

world.place: the rail town two valleys east of the carpeted village (Light Sleeper); its line runs south over a river bridge through the hills toward Grandma's sister's village
world.easter_egg: S09 (the dawn crane over the line): the carpeted village of Light Sleeper on a far hill at frame left, carpet roofs in red and orange, the bell boxed in white wool. Provisional: re-check against docs/world/canon.md when it lands.

requests.direction: A bright, fast nine-year-old boy tells his friends an amazing true story about his grandpa: quick, excited, full volume, a grin in his voice even in the sad parts, a short breath between sentences; never whispery or breathy.

lines.text: My grandpa / has waited for / the SAME MINECART / for TWENTY-TWO / YEARS.
lines.direction: one quick breath, bright and amazed, a tiny lift on the number

lines.text: Every EVENING. / Empty RAIL. / He just says, / "She's COMING."
lines.say: Every evening. Empty rail. <short pause> He just says, "She's coming."
lines.direction: matter-of-fact, then quoting him plainly and fondly, no impression of an old voice

lines.text: Our PIG / lives in / his CART. / He LOVES it.
lines.direction: proud and cheerful, sure of it

lines.text: Won't even / get out / for a CARROT.
lines.direction: laughing at how silly the pig is

lines.text: Mom said / Grandma LEFT him. / Went to her SISTER'S. / Never came BACK.
lines.direction: the grin drops a notch, still full volume, repeating what grown-ups say
indignant on the last word, a kid taking Grandpa's side

lines.text: Villagers / never leave / the VILLAGE. / And I wasn't / allowed past / the BRIDGE.
lines.direction: explaining the rules fast, a little fed up with the second one

lines.text: At MIDNIGHT / I turned TEN. / I packed RAILS / and WENT.
lines.direction: lit up and brave, speeding up, the big moment
big and a little out of breath, impressed with himself

lines.text: Then the rail / STOPPED. / A CREEPER hole, / all grassed OVER.
lines.direction: a sudden stop in the voice on the second phrase, then puzzled, still full volume

lines.text: Past it, / a MINECART. / GRANDMA / in it. / Still facing HOME.
lines.direction: the speed goes out of him; wonder, not sadness; a beat before the last phrase, which lands warm

lines.text: I bridged / the HOLE, / laid RAILS, / and PUSHED.
lines.direction: fast and determined, building speed to the last word like a launch

lines.text: That EVENING, / Grandpa was / waiting. / Like ALWAYS.
lines.direction: gentle and proud, smiling, full volume, slowing only on the last two words
warm and a little sheepish, a smile in it, as if she missed the bus
